subject: getting a shiny package to pass R CMD check

messages.author: 8be0609cdf98caa5
messages.subject: getting a shiny package to pass R CMD check
parts:
In the shiny tutorial it states to export a function containing something like:

shiny::runApp(system.file('appdir', package='packagename'))


if you want to create a package that you can share, so that others can run your shiny tool locally.

I've done this, and my package is running on my machine, but I'm failing some R CMD checks.

I only have one function that I export and it looks like:

webtool <- function(){

  shiny::runApp(system.file('webtool', package = 'pqantimalarials'))
 
}

My CMD check warnings and errors are below. I am wondering why I get the S3 generic/method inconsistency (#1), and what my \usage section needs to look like for my webtool function since it has no input parameters (#2).

This might be more appropriate for the r-devel list, but many thanks for any help.

---

#1
* checking S3 generic/method consistency ... WARNING
Error in Context$new : could not find function "loadMethod"
Calls: <Anonymous> ... unlist -> lapply -> FUN -> .is_S3_generic -> get -> $
Execution halted
See section ‘Generic functions and methods’ of the ‘Writing R

# 2
* checking Rd \usage sections ... NOTE
Error in Context$new : could not find function "loadMethod"
Calls: <Anonymous> ... unlist -> lapply -> FUN -> .is_S3_generic -> get -> $
Execution halted
The \usage entries for S3 methods should use the \method markup and not
their full name.
See the chapter ‘Writing R documentation files’ in the ‘Writing R
Extensions’ manual.

# 3
* checking PDF version of manual ... WARNING
LaTeX errors when creating PDF version.
This typically indicates Rd problems.

# 4
* checking PDF version of manual without hyperrefs or index ... ERROR
Re-running with no redirection of stdout/stderr.
Hmm ... looks like a package
Error in texi2dvi(file = file, pdf = TRUE, clean = clean, quiet = quiet,  :
  pdflatex is not available
Error in running tools::texi2pdf()

parts:
1) Roxygen will write methods to the namespace if you have a #'@imports methods I did suggest this see post #5 ;) . There were changes in R 3.02 here are the relevant NEWS items 
* R CMD check does more thorough checking of declared packages and
      namespaces.  It reports

        * packages declared in more than one of the Depends, Imports,
          Suggests and Enhances fields of the DESCRIPTION file.

        * namespaces declared in Imports but not imported from, neither
          in the NAMESPACE file nor using the :: nor ::: operators.

        * packages which are used in library() or requires() calls in
          the R code but were already put on the search path _via_
          Depends.

        * packages declared in Depends not imported _via_ the NAMESPACE
          file (except the standard packages).  Objects used from
          Depends packages should be imported to avoid conflicts and to
          allow correct operation when the namespace is loaded but not
          attached.

2) No idea to be honest it is all rather confusing

3) Some of the packages you are importing namely

shiny,
    reshape2,
    RColorBrewer,
    rms,
    plyr

depend on methods. You are importing all of them and maybe need to be depending on some of them instead.

Josh O Brien explains it

"There is one unfortunately common exception to the advice above: if your package relies on a package A which itself "Depends" on another package B, your package will likely need to attach A with a "Depends directive.

This is because the functions in package A were written with the expectation that package B and its functions would be attached to the search() path."

from http://stackoverflow.com/questions/8637993/better-explanation-of-when-to-use-imports-depends
